beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent. You share its context, a skill, its output or an interface, and the choice between them is a strategy decision.
beats.got: There are four things you can hand over and I'm told to choose between them. I don't know yet what I'd be choosing for.

beats.trigger: Bring one example from your own organisation of a tool people were given access to and then did not use.
beats.got: I can use my own case. We bought licences for a reporting add-in and the controllers kept their Excel files.

beats.trigger: **Identify** the absorption bottleneck that decides whether the teammate takes the candidate up
beats.got: nothing new. It's a list of verbs and I can't tell what any of it costs.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to actually have: your folder, one of your skills, the output on a schedule, or a way to ask it a question in Slack?
beats.got: I'm supposed to have a challenge memory and a folder from earlier modules. I'm not sure what I'm picking from. I'd have to guess.

beats.trigger: Hold the impulse. Then start with the teammate's work.
beats.got: The point is to start from the teammate's job, not from the tool. That's reasonable, but the intro is long and has no figure in it.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: A test I can apply: a vague answer is a bad answer. The agent reads my files and writes up one teammate's job. I could check that.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: That is how our IT picks tools, and it's what I'd want to challenge. The reason for a pick has to be the outcome.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a handoff to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: This exercise is about what would stop the teammate using it, and a plan in two halves.

beats.trigger: The obstacle is usually not the first technical limitation a builder sees.
beats.got: The thing that blocks adoption is usually not the technical limit. My add-in case fits: nobody had a reason to switch. It only takes five minutes, so I'd stay for it.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: Unnamed owners count as a finding. That is a risk named before I have to raise it, and I'd use it on any project plan. There is still no cost line anywhere in it.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: Buying a tool because it fits our systems is shopping. Picking one because it moves an outcome is design. That is a rule I can apply to our purchases.

beats.trigger: Whether they do gets settled outside the files, in their week.
beats.got: Whether people use it gets decided in their working week, not in the plan.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
beats.got: Someone has to answer for what the agent does, and a vendor's 'shared agent' doesn't include that person. It's a fair point against vendors but abstract, and I had to read it twice.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.

take_homes: Seats bought is not use. I'd ask for usage figures next to the licence count.
Before we buy or roll out a tool, ask what it replaces for a named person and what would make them stop using the old way. If the answer is 'we already have the platform', that is shopping.
A plan with unnamed owners is not finished. The unassigned roles are the findings.

monday.move: Ask my controller how she does the month-end variance commentary today, and show her nothing yet. I'd also pull actual usage against the licence count for the reporting add-in.
monday.who: My controller, plus whoever in IT holds the add-in licence data
monday.stop_condition: If she can't describe a step the agent would improve, I stop. If IT has no usage data, I note that as the finding.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved any AI tool for finance data, so I can't let her try anything on real figures, and I can't put a cost per month on it.

misconception.why: I came in thinking AI is a licence you buy. The point that access takes a minute while absorption happens in other people's weeks matches my add-in case, so I now see the part the licence doesn't cover. I'm not convinced it's a capability the organisation builds. I never saw a cost or payback figure, so I'd still call it unproven.

one_line: Useful for stopping us buying seats and calling it adoption. It didn't give me a single figure for the board.
